ai.description: This skink reaches 18 cm total length. It is bronze-brown with a distinct dark lateral stripe bordered by white spots. It features smooth scales and a transparent lower eyelid window.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Sphenomorphus indicus* is the presence of a distinct, continuous dark lateral band that extends from the snout through the eye to the tail.
ai.habitat: *Sphenomorphus indicus* inhabits moist, shaded leaf litter in subtropical broadleaf forests and dense riparian zones, typically ranging from 500 to 2,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Indian Forest Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphenomorphus indicus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer monsoon months, generally between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Forest Skink occurs in Northeast India, primarily in the Eastern Himalayas and Assam, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 2,000 meters in elevation.
